newsitem.title: CHINA: Friendship '96 volume up, profit do.
newsitem.headline: Friendship '96 volume up, profit do.

text.p: Shanghai Friendship and Overseas Chinese Co will post higher turnover for 1996 against 1995 but lower post-tax profit, said a research paper given Reuters by Shenyin & Wanguo on Tuesday.
The paper said the reduction was partly due to rising costs resulting from changes in acccounting policies in China in the past three years.
China's securities rules require listed firms to post their previous year's results before April 30. Friendship has yet to report the results.

In 1997, the company is expected to improve its performance with the opening of a new shop, Friendship Maosheng Gift Store, at the end of 1996, the research paper said. The company has a 60 percent stake in the shop.

Also, the first of a planned chain of 10 joint venture retail shops will open in May 1997 with all 10 expected to be in operation within two years. The company has a 50 percent stake in the venture with the rest belonging to its Japanese partners.
Friendship plans to issue shares to fund new projects, the research paper said. It recommended that investors hold the company's shares and wait for better opportunities.
